description: The thin MFC UI sibling (hammer.adapters.mfc) built with the real MSVC+MFC toolchain and verified under Wine. This is a NEW thin shell (not the legacy Hammer MFC shell), parallel to the GTK sibling: it depends only on MFC + the reusable, engine-free editor libraries, so unlike the legacy shell it builds and links against the extracted libraries alone -- no tier0/vgui2/materialsystem. This sidesteps the D2 blocker, which was specific to the legacy shell's whole-engine dependency. LOCAL gate: the MSVC+MFC toolchain (mstorsjo/msvc-wine, atlmfc) is a large licensed install and is not in CI; the reproducible CI Windows lane for the MFC-free core remains MinGW+Wine (hammer_windows_parity.json).
compiler: Microsoft (R) C/C++ Optimizing Compiler 19.29.30159 (VS2019 v142, toolset 14.29.30133 with atlmfc)
mfc: shared MFC (mfc140.dll, /MD /D_AFXDLL); mfc140.dll present in the Wine prefix

artifacts.detail: Thin MFC GUI sibling (CWinApp + CFrameWnd + programmatic menu; command handlers delegate to EditorDocument + DiskFileStore) compiles and links to a real PE32+ GUI executable against MFC + the reusable library sources and nothing else. A GUI needs a display to run (as with the GTK shell); the compile+link is the sibling-exists proof.

Console MFC-linked binary (afx.h + CString touch-point) RUNS under Wine and exercises the delegated New -> SetKey -> Save -> reopen -> Undo/Redo workflow through EditorDocument + the real DiskFileStore. Proves MFC and the reusable engine-free libraries link and coexist in one binary and the workflow executes correctly at runtime -- a stronger runtime proof than the GTK sibling's (which runs without the toolkit).

scope: Proves a NEW thin MFC sibling builds against MFC + the reusable libraries and its editing workflow runs under Wine. Does NOT build the legacy Hammer MFC shell (afxwin CMapDoc/CMapView entangled with the whole Source Windows engine), which remains windows-mfc-legacy=unverified. Running the MFC GUI (message loop, windows) needs a display and is not covered here; full H5 editor feature parity is future work.
siblingSymmetry: Both UI siblings now build on the same reusable libraries: hammer.adapters.gtk (GTK4/libadwaita, hammer_windows_parity.json + adapters.gtk_shell.v1) and hammer.adapters.mfc (MFC, this artifact + adapters.mfc_shell.v1). Both persist through hammer::adapters::platform::DiskFileStore and serialize via hammer::formats; neither contains editor policy.
